spec.description: The observation one station reported at one exact moment.

station_id.description: Station identifier, such as `KSEA`. `stations.list_stations` returns it as `stationIdentifier`.

time.description: When the observation was taken, to the second. It must be the `timestamp` of an observation the station reported: the service does not round to the nearest one, and answers 404 for a moment between two. It keeps about a week, and answers 404 for anything older.

response.title: TimedObservationFeature
response.description: The observation, in the GeoJSON feature the API wraps it in. The geometry repeats the station's own coordinates, which `properties` already identifies, so the client hands back `properties`.

notes: Measured 2026-09-30 at KSEA, which reports every five minutes and a METAR at :53: `20:53:00Z` and `21:05:00Z` answered, `20:30:00Z` answered 404, and so did `2026-09-23T21:00:00Z` while `2026-09-24T21:00:00Z` still answered. A `time` with an offset (`14:00:00-07:00`) names the same observation as its UTC form.
`refresh_examples.py` repoints the example to the newest METAR in the settled observation window before every re-recording, since the one it names ages out within a week.
